﻿# Architecture Review Board

**← Back to [EAP Home](../../README.md) • [Governance](../README.md) • [Governing Bodies](./README.md)**

> Gate 3 governing body responsible for enterprise architecture alignment, design validation, and formal architectural approval for projects involving new technologies or significant enterprise impact.

[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#governing-body-overview]

## Governing Body Overview

**Purpose**: Enterprise architecture alignment, design validation, and formal architectural approval for projects involving new technologies, architectural changes, or significant enterprise impact.

**Charter**: The Architecture Review Board (ARB) serves as Gate 3 in the governance framework, providing comprehensive architectural approval for all projects requiring architectural review after successful domain-specific validation. The ARB ensures alignment with enterprise strategy and adherence to architectural standards.

**Body Type**: Decision-Making (has formal authority to approve, reject, or mandate changes)

**Gate Authority**: Gate 3 - Architecture Review Board Process in the 6-gate governance framework

**GainwellNow Enterprise Architecture Governance**: [Submit CRB Request](https://gainwellnow.service-now.com/esc?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=3d2faedac356ce908978decf050131f6)

[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#when-an-arb-input-form-is-required]

### When an ARB Input Form Is Required

An [ARB Input Form](../../resources/work-templates/governance/README.md#architecture-review-board-arb) must be submitted when **either** of the following applies:

- **Project-based path**: The project has received CRB (Gate 1) approval, is assessed as **Medium or High risk** with **cross-domain** impact per the architecture governance [Gate Requirements and Criteria](../processes/architecture-governance.md#23-gate-requirements-and-criteria), and its detailed solution design meets one or more of the Qualifying Activities below. The ARB intake initiates DRB (Gate 2): the Security Domain Review is mandatory for every ARB submission, and the AI Domain Review additionally applies when the solution involves AI/ML; DRB approval is required before the formal ARB review. Not every CRB-approved initiative requires ARB submission; only those that meet the risk/impact threshold **and** whose design triggers a qualifying activity must proceed to final architectural design review and implementation approval. This includes the same project/request types evaluated at CRB:

  - **New Product/Service**: Net-new solutions, platforms, or customer/state-facing capabilities
  - **Product Enhancement**: Material functional, integration, or architectural changes to an existing solution
  - **Technical Request**: Adoption of new technology platforms, major version upgrades, or infrastructure changes with architectural impact

- **Standards-mandated path**: An active enterprise standard, pattern, or governance policy independently requires ARB approval for a specific request — such as a standards exception, a new taxonomy or qualifier addition, or another standards-governed decision — regardless of CRB approval, risk rating, or domain impact (for example, [STD-GOV-GP-001](../../standards/governance/STD-GOV-GP-001-golden-path-catalog-naming-standard.md#exception-management-process) requires ARB approval for new Golden Path language qualifiers). Submit directly to ARB per the mandating standard's own exception process.
page_texts.6:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#qualifying-activities]

### Qualifying Activities

Among initiatives meeting the Medium/High risk, cross-domain threshold above, an ARB submission is required when the detailed solution design involves **one or more** of the following:

- ✅ New product offering
- ✅ Major modifications to an existing product offering
- ✅ New or materially changed system architecture (application components, services, or platforms)
- ✅ New or materially changed data architecture (data models, storage, or data flows)
- ✅ New or materially changed infrastructure architecture (compute, network, or hosting environments)
- ✅ New or materially changed security architecture (controls, authentication, or authorization)
- ✅ New or materially changed integration architecture (APIs, messaging, or cross-system data exchange)
- ✅ Adoption of new technologies not already part of the approved enterprise technology stack
- ✅ Adoption of new platforms not already part of the approved enterprise technology stack
- ✅ Adoption of new vendor products not already part of the approved enterprise technology stack
- ✅ Integration patterns crossing multiple systems
- ✅ Integration patterns crossing multiple domains
- ✅ Integration patterns crossing external parties
- ✅ Requests for exceptions to enterprise architecture standards
- ✅ Requests for exceptions to enterprise technology standards
- ✅ Security architecture changes requiring the Security Domain Input Addendum (from the DRB Security Domain Review)
- ✅ AI/ML architecture changes requiring the AI Domain Input Addendum (from the DRB AI Domain Review)
- ✅ Material changes to a previously CRB/DRB-approved conceptual or domain design
page_texts.7:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#when-arb-submission-is-not-required]

### When ARB Submission Is Not Required

Under the project-based path, ARB submission is not required when an initiative does not meet the **Medium or High risk with cross-domain impact** threshold, regardless of qualifying activities, or when an initiative meets that threshold but its detailed solution design meets **none** of the qualifying activities above. Routine maintenance, break/fix work, and configuration-only changes that do not alter the approved architecture are therefore exempt under this path. This exemption does not override the standards-mandated path above — a request for which an active standard, pattern, or governance policy independently requires ARB approval still requires submission regardless of project risk rating, domain impact, or qualifying activities. When in doubt, consult the assigned Solution Architect or the EA Governance Coordinator to confirm applicability before proceeding.

page_texts.9:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#required-information]

### Required Information

- **Detailed Architecture Design**: Comprehensive solution architecture with all technical components
- **Design Documentation**: Architecture diagrams, design decisions, and technical specifications
- **Risk Assessment**: Detailed risk analysis with mitigation strategies
- **Compliance Checklist**: Validation of adherence to enterprise standards and policies
- **Technology Selection Justification**: Rationale for technology choices and vendor selections
- **Integration Architecture**: Integration patterns, APIs, and data flow specifications
- **Security Architecture**: Security controls, authentication, authorization, and compliance requirements using the Security Domain Input Addendum
- **AI Architecture**: AI/ML model design, responsible AI considerations, and governance requirements using the AI Domain Input Addendum
- **Implementation Plan**: Detailed implementation approach, timeline, and resource requirements
page_texts.10:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#decision-criteria]

### Decision Criteria

- **Standards Compliance**: Full adherence to enterprise architecture standards and policies
- **Technical Feasibility**: Validated technical approach with proven technologies and patterns
- **Integration Alignment**: Proper integration patterns and enterprise service bus utilization
- **Security & Compliance**: Comprehensive security controls and regulatory compliance
- **Scalability & Performance**: Architecture supports required scale and performance targets
- **Vendor & Technology Fit**: Appropriate technology selections aligned with enterprise roadmap
- **Risk Mitigation**: Acceptable risk profile with documented mitigation strategies
- **Resource Availability**: Confirmed availability of required technical resources and expertise

---
page_texts.12:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#primary-activities]

### Primary Activities

- **Architecture Review**: Evaluate detailed solution architectures for standards compliance
- **Technology Validation**: Assess technology selections and vendor choices
- **Design Approval**: Validate architectural designs and implementation approaches
- **Standards Enforcement**: Ensure adherence to enterprise architecture standards and policies
- **Risk Assessment**: Review and validate technical risk assessments and mitigation plans
- **Integration Oversight**: Validate integration patterns and enterprise connectivity
- **Compliance Verification**: Ensure regulatory and security compliance requirements are met
- **Implementation Guidance**: Provide architectural guidance during implementation
page_texts.13:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#key-deliverables]

### Key Deliverables

- **Architecture Approval Decisions**: Formal approval, conditional approval, or rejection decisions
- **Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)**: Documentation of significant architectural decisions
- **Standards Compliance Validation**: Verification of adherence to enterprise standards
- **Risk Mitigation Plans**: Approved risk mitigation strategies and action plans
- **Implementation Recommendations**: Guidance and recommendations for implementation
- **Compliance Certifications**: Validation of regulatory and security compliance
page_texts.14:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#review-scope]

### Review Scope

The ARB evaluates projects for:

- **Architecture Standards**: Compliance with enterprise architecture standards and patterns
- **Technology Alignment**: Technology selections aligned with enterprise technology roadmap
- **Integration Architecture**: Proper integration patterns, APIs, and data exchange mechanisms
- **Security Architecture**: Security controls, authentication, authorization, and data protection (Reviewed during the Security Domain Review)
- **AI Architecture**: AI/ML model governance, responsible AI principles, data bias, and explainability (Reviewed during the AI Domain Review)
- **Performance & Scalability**: Architecture supports required performance and scale requirements
- **Vendor & Technology**: Vendor selections and technology choices aligned with enterprise strategy
- **Risk Management**: Comprehensive risk assessment with acceptable mitigation strategies
- **Implementation Readiness**: Validated implementation approach with confirmed resources

---
page_texts.16:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#gateway-flow]

### Gateway Flow

- **Input**: Approved concepts from CRB (Gate 1) and DRB (Gate 2) with detailed architectural designs
- **Process**: Architecture review, design validation, standards compliance verification, technology assessment
- **Output**: Approved architectures proceed to Development Implementation (Gate 4)
- **Rejection**: Architectures not meeting criteria are returned for remediation
page_texts.17:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#exit-criteria]

### Exit Criteria

Projects approved by ARB must demonstrate:

- Full compliance with enterprise architecture standards
- Validated technical design with proven technologies
- Comprehensive security and compliance controls
- Acceptable risk profile with mitigation strategies
- Approved integration architecture and patterns
- Confirmed resource availability and implementation plan
- Documented architectural decisions in ADRs

[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#submission-process]

## Submission Process

Steps 1–9 below describe the full intake for **project-based** ARB requests (ARB Input Document, SDR Input Addendum, and — if applicable — AIDR Input Addendum). **Standards-mandated** requests (see [Applicability](#when-an-arb-input-form-is-required)) instead follow the abbreviated intake defined by the mandating standard — typically a PR with a documented justification — in place of the ARB Input Document and AIDR Input Addendum. Regardless of path, the Security Domain Review (Step 6) is mandatory before the Formal ARB Review (Step 8): the mandating standard's exception process must route the request through Security Domain Review before ARB approval is requested.
page_texts.20:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-1-prepare-input-documents]

### Step 1: Prepare Input Documents

Prepare the ARB Input Document and the SDR (Security Domain Review) Input Addendum based on the templates. Solutions that include AI also require an AIDR (AI Domain Review) Input Addendum. **Retain a personal copy of each document.**

Templates must be fully completed:

- No sections or tables may be removed
- Where a section is not applicable, state "N/A" along with the justification
- All placeholder text marked in brackets (`[ ]`) must be completed

Templates: [Architecture Review Board (ARB) Templates](../../resources/work-templates/governance/README.md#architecture-review-board-arb)
page_texts.21:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-2-run-the-ai-governance-report]

### Step 2: Run the AI Governance Report

Use the [AI Reviewer](https://ea-reference.tools.mgt.pgwcloud.net/ai-reviewer/) tool to evaluate documentation for clarity, completeness, and alignment with EA standards and guidelines. Documentation should score at least 80% with no HIGH or BLOCKER findings. This tool is in proof-of-concept — use the "Rate this Review" option at the bottom of the report to provide feedback and help improve accuracy.
page_texts.22:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-3-peer-review]

### Step 3: Peer Review

Peer review all Input Documents with the assigned team before submission.
page_texts.23:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-4-submit-arb-request]

### Step 4: Submit ARB Request

Submit the ARB request with the ARB Input Document, the SDR Input Addendum, and (if applicable) the AIDR Input Addendum via [Gainwell ARB Intake (GainwellNow)](https://gainwellnow.service-now.com/esc?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=3d2faedac356ce908978decf050131f6). Use the external login option and enter a Gainwell Technologies email address.
page_texts.24:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-5-completeness-validation]

### Step 5: Completeness Validation

The ARB Chair validates the submission for completeness. All required documentation must be submitted, and the ARB Input Document must score 80% or higher on the AI Reviewer tool with no BLOCKER or HIGH mandatory changes outstanding. Only a submission deemed complete moves forward to the Security Domain Review. The submitter receives an email indicating whether changes are required — if not, instructions follow to schedule the Security Domain Review and any other required Domain Reviews.
page_texts.25:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-6-domain-reviews]

### Step 6: Domain Reviews

Attend the Security Domain Review with Security Team members to present the case and receive feedback to incorporate into the ARB Input Document. If other Domain Reviews are required (e.g., AI Domain Review), schedule them and obtain approvals.
page_texts.26:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-7-upload-domain-review-results]

### Step 7: Upload Domain Review Results

Upload the post-Domain-Review updated documentation and approvals to the GainwellNow ticket.

> **Note**: The ARB ID is the GainwellNow ticket's RITM number. This is a good time to update the ARB Input Document with the RITM number.
page_texts.27:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-8-formal-arb-review]

### Step 8: Formal ARB Review

Once the initial review is complete and the updated ARB Input and Domain Review Addendum documents are uploaded, an invitation to the Formal ARB Review session follows to present the ARB Input Document for approval. ARB meetings are held weekly on Thursday ET; the meeting agenda is sent on Tuesdays. To be included on the agenda, an issue-free ARB Input Document with all required security and other domain review approvals must be uploaded to the GainwellNow ticket by Tuesday morning ET.
page_texts.28:
[governance/governing-bodies/architecture-review-board.md#step-9-post-meeting-disposition]

### Step 9: Post-Meeting Disposition

- **Approved**: The ARB is marked **FINAL** and **APPROVED**, and the Build and Test Phase may proceed.
- **Deferred**: If additional action items are required, the ARB is **deferred** and remains in pending status until the ARB Input Document is updated with the mandatory action items. Upload the updated ARB Input Document with track changes enabled and the version/change log history updated. Once changes are validated for correctness, a return to Formal ARB to present the updates may be requested, or approval may arrive via email. Once approved, the ARB is marked **FINAL** and **APPROVED**, and the Build and Test Phase may proceed.
